page: Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial, totaling 768.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 16.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), and cryptographic acceleration extensions. This instance type includes no local storage and does not bundle hardware GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional performance in memory-intensive and parallel processing workloads. The instance achieves strong memory bandwidth results, recording 337.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 3721.94 GB/sec for cached small-block operations. In compute and system workloads, it posts a Geekbench multi-core score of 18792.0 and a PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 70186.64. Database capabilities are emphasized by a PassMark database operations metric of 27022.32 and 66.87 million Redis SET operations per second. While multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into the top 25% of measured systems, raw stress-ng CPU metrics align within the middle 50% average.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to the constrained vCPU-to-memory ratio. By provisioning 48 vCPUs alongside the full 768.0 GB memory footprint typically associated with a 96-vCPU instance chassis, the E96-48s_v6 reduces per-core software licensing costs while retaining substantial RAM. A key architectural tradeoff is the total lack of bundled local storage, requiring external networked block storage for persistent data, and the absence of discrete GPUs for accelerated machine learning training.

Given its high memory density, robust memory throughput, and dedicated core configuration, Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v6 is well aligned for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor reaching 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 768.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high 16.0 GB per core ratio supported by a 260 MB L3 cache and AMX matrix instructions. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the E96-48s_v6 demonstrates top-quartile performance in memory bandwidth (337.64 GB/sec uncached reads), software compilation, and in-memory key-value processing, logging 66.87 million Redis SET operations per second. The constrained core configuration optimizes database licensing expenses relative to available RAM capacity. It is primarily suited for large in-memory caching layers, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics, and memory-bound transactional workloads.
